meta.origin: Measured tier: Yahoo Finance batch spark endpoint (v7/finance/spark, range=1y&interval=1d). Index tier: the SEC company_tickers_exchange.json listed-issuer file.
meta.note: Offline starting point, NOT a quote. Every ticker, fund and company name here is real. Prices, trailing yields, volatility and the movementStats block are approximate round figures for 2026-08-01, hand-set to be plainly reasonable rather than precise. movementStats has exactly the shape core/movement.js analyse() returns, so the setup, heat and expected-move band shown offline are computed by the same code that runs on refresh. Classification, mutual-fund minimums and access notes come from MEASURED_UNIVERSE in src/sources/equities.js, not from this file. The `series` array on each row is an illustrative shape, not a price history: see fields.series. It exists so a chart drawn offline agrees with the statistics beside it.

fields.symbol: ticker; must exist in the adapter MEASURED_UNIVERSE or the row is skipped
fields.price: share or NAV price in USD; also the minimum investment unless the fund sets one
fields.trailingYield: sum of the last 12 months of distributions over price, percent. 0 means it genuinely pays nothing
fields.maxDrawdown: deepest peak-to-trough fall over the window, percent — a risk input
fields.movementStats: precomputed chart read: vol, regime{recent,baseline,ratio}, rangePos, drawdown, trend, volumeRatio, lastClose, bars
fields.series: 60 evenly-spaced points ending at this row's price, for the offline chart. NOT recorded closes: an illustrative shape derived from the movementStats above so the chart cannot contradict the numbers printed beside it — the last point IS lastClose, the peak sits exactly `drawdown` percent above it, the low sits where `rangePos` says it does, and the last quarter of the series moves at `trend` per month. Where those figures cannot all be true at once (a row 1% off its high and 99% up its range implies a low below zero) the drawdown and the trend win, because a chart that climbs while the row says it is falling is the one inconsistency nobody would forgive. Live, this field is real closes from the price feed, thinned the same way.

meta.secSampleNote: A 62-row sample of the SEC listed-issuer file in the shape that endpoint publishes, so the two-tier UI has unmeasured rows to render offline. These carry identity only — no price, no rate, nothing measured. CIK is present only where it can be stated exactly; the live file always carries one. Live, this tier covers about 10,000 issuers.
